newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Agrobanka posts loss before provisions.
newsitem.headline: Agrobanka posts loss before provisions.

text.p: Troubled Czech Agrobanka a.s., under central bank administration since last year, posted a preliminary 1996 loss of 200 million crowns before the creation of reserves and provisions, the administrator said on Friday.

Jiri Klumpar, who took control of Agrobanka after it suffered a liquidity crisis last summer, told a news conference that he was continuing efforts to reduce total net losses by keeping the bank functioning.
"An independent audit had confirmed losses of (Agrobanka) before the imposition of forced administration (last September) totalling 10 billion crowns," said Klumpar.
Agrobank, at the time of the forced administration, was the country's largest fully private bank, and fifth largest overall.
The central bank had already rejected a demand by a major shareholder of the bank, the investment group Motoinvest, to liquidate.
"The option (of liquidating the bank) could deepen the existing losses. In this option I would expect losses of several tens of billions of crowns," Klumpar said.
Klumpar is leading a plan to split Agrobanka's questionable assets away from quality holdings and then sell a controlling stake in the bank based on a balance sheet holding only the good assets.
Officials have yet to say what would become of the questionable assets.
A central bank guarantee on all deposits in the bank remains in place as Agrobanka continues its operations.
The London office of HSBC Investment Bank won the central bank's mandate earlier this year to arrange the selloff of a majority stake in Agrobanka to a strategic foreign investor.
